title: Étale localizations preserve dimension
statement: If $A\to B$ is an étale map of commutative rings, $q$ is a prime ideal of $B$, and $p$ is its inverse image in $A$, then $\dim(A_p)=\dim(B_q)$, with Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QP (Lemma 44.2), dimension of local rings under an étale map

proof.text: The localization map $A_p\to B_q$ is flat and local by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps]: the first node gives flatness of the etale map $A\to B$, and the second gives the induced flat local map on localizations. Hence it is faithfully flat by [lem-pc-local-flat-faithful-flat-reflects-surjective]. Applying [lem-sc-faithfully-flat-local-dimension] gives $\dim(A_p)\le\dim(B_q)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QP, proof, first paragraph: the localized etale map is flat, hence going down, giving the lower dimension inequality

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-quasi-finite], the etale ring map $A\to B$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at $q$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-inequality-quasi-finite], applied to $q$ and its contraction $p$, gives $\dim(B_q)\le\dim(A_p)$. Combining the two inequalities proves equality.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QP, proof, second paragraph: etale maps are quasi-finite and strict prime chains contract, giving the reverse inequality
